claim_scope: success rates are not directly comparable when task populations, success definitions, or denominators differ
a benchmark card should expose protocol differences before ranking models
a small-sample point estimate should be accompanied by an uncertainty interval under explicit assumptions
valid truncations remain in a frozen denominator while declared technical-invalid attempts block aggregation instead of disappearing
a factorial protocol audit can expose interaction and prevent warning labels from being misread as additive causal effects
paired route-level analysis can separate episode-micro and equal-route-macro estimands while preserving within-pair comparisons
zero observed events retain a positive one-sided binomial risk upper bound under explicit independent-trial assumptions
repeated members within authored route clusters do not create independent routes, and episode-event versus cluster-incidence bounds answer different estimands
selecting a checkpoint on a final score reassigns that split to model selection; an untouched authored confirmation score can expose the resulting reuse gap without estimating expected selection bias
identical candidate and baseline marginal success rates do not determine their paired joint table, discordant-pair count, or a predeclared exact conditional McNemar diagnostic

code.config: standard-library fixed episode-table, paired-margin, checkpoint-selection, zero-event, pseudoreplication, and paired route-cluster protocol audit

data.name: procedural episode, paired-route, paired-margin, checkpoint-selection, and zero-event pseudoreplication audit tables

limitations: fixed hand-authored outcomes rather than simulator rollouts

Wilson intervals and zero-event upper bounds apply only to their explicitly declared independent Bernoulli units; episode-event and cluster-incidence probabilities are different estimands, not alternative corrections for one parameter
the factorial effects are arithmetic contrasts on authored rows, not population causal-effect estimates
the four-route exact bootstrap and percentile interval demonstrate mechanics but are too small and authored for calibrated population inference
the paired-margin exact conditional diagnostic has no effect-size interval, cluster or multiplicity correction, equivalence margin, or population-sampling claim
the four-checkpoint score table is deliberately authored and does not estimate expected selection bias, checkpoint quality, or model generalization
does not estimate any real policy or benchmark performance
the injected invalid-run case tests rejection only and does not estimate a technical failure rate
